slides.title: Competitor Landscape Update: Zumilokibart (APG777)
slides.subtitle: Atopic Dermatitis — APEX Phase 2 Part B 16-Week Data (May 2026)
slides.speakerNotes: This deck summarizes the zumilokibart (APG777) APEX Phase 2 Part B readout in moderate-to-severe AD from Apogee Therapeutics. Zumilokibart is a next-generation anti-IL-13 mAb designed for extended dosing intervals (Q12W–Q24W). Key question: does it threaten lebrikizumab's positioning as a differentiated IL-13 biologic? The mid dose is the selected Phase 3 dose. Data released May 27, 2026.

slides.title: Drug Overview: Zumilokibart (APG777)

bullets: Generic: zumilokibart | Code: APG777 | Sponsor: Apogee Therapeutics
Modality: Humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody (engineered Fc for extended half-life)
Target: IL-13 (high-affinity)
Route: Subcutaneous injection
Dosing: Induction Wk 0, 2, 4, 12 (4 dosing days) → Maintenance Q12W (high) or Q24W (mid = planned Ph3 dose)
Phase: Phase 2 Part B completed; Phase 3 (ADventure) initiation expected 2H 2026
Same MOA class as lebrikizumab (anti-IL-13) — direct competitor
Key differentiator: extended dosing (2–4 injections/year vs 26 for Dupixent, 13 for lebrikizumab)
Numerically highest EASI-75 at Wk16 among all anti-IL-13/IL-4 biologics (cross-trial, Ph2 MCMC-MI)
Rapid onset: significance by Week 2 for all dose groups
If confirmed in Phase 3 with NRI, positions as potential best-in-class convenience

slides.speakerNotes: Apogee Therapeutics was founded to develop extended half-life biologics for chronic diseases. Zumilokibart uses engineered Fc to extend half-life, allowing quarterly dosing. The competitive threat is primarily to lebrikizumab (same target) but also to the broader biologic class if convenience drives switching.

slides.title: Mechanism of Action: Anti-IL-13

bullets: IL-13 is a key type 2 cytokine driving AD pathophysiology: barrier disruption, inflammation, pruritus
Zumilokibart neutralizes IL-13 with high affinity — prevents binding to IL-13Rα1/IL-4Rα receptor complex
Same target as lebrikizumab and tralokinumab; different from dupilumab (IL-4Rα blocks both IL-4 and IL-13)

sections.header: Key Differentiators vs Existing IL-13 Therapies
bullets: Engineered IgG1 Fc for extended half-life → enables Q12W–Q24W dosing (vs Q2W–Q4W for lebrikizumab/tralokinumab)
Higher binding affinity claimed (prevents dissociation during extended dosing interval)
Same fundamental mechanism — efficacy differentiation likely driven by PK/dosing rather than biology
Potential risk: longer half-life means slower washout if adverse events occur

slides.speakerNotes: The MOA is essentially identical to lebrikizumab — both selectively block IL-13. The differentiation is entirely PK-driven: engineered Fc extends half-life from ~2 weeks (typical IgG1) to estimated 4-6 weeks, enabling quarterly dosing. If anti-IL-13 monotherapy works, the one requiring fewest injections wins on convenience.

slides.title: Study Design: APEX Phase 2 Part B

bullets: Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
N = 346 (mITT); 1:1:1:1 to High/Mid/Low dose + Placebo
Population: Moderate-to-severe AD (EASI ≥16, vIGA ≥3, BSA ≥10%)
Monotherapy (no background TCS required)
Primary endpoint: EASI-75 at Week 16
Key secondary: IGA 0/1, EASI-90, EASI-100, I-NRS4 at Week 16
Mid dose = selected Phase 3 dose (N=85 vs N=88 PBO)
Missing data: MCMC-MI (more lenient than NRI in competitor Ph3s)

slides.speakerNotes: APEX Part B enrolled moderate-to-severe AD patients (EASI≥16, vIGA≥3, BSA≥10%). N=346 (mITT) randomized 1:1:1:1. Induction: 4 dosing days (Wk0, 2, 4, 12). Maintenance: High dose Q12W, Mid dose Q24W. Primary endpoint: EASI-75 at Week 16. Rescue medication use/discontinuation = non-response.
slides.disclaimer: Source: Apogee Therapeutics APEX Part B data presentation, May 27, 2026. Review is required before disclosure.

slides.title: Dosing Convenience: Zumilokibart vs Dupixent
slides.speakerNotes: Key commercial differentiator: Zumilokibart induction requires 4 dosing days (Wk 0, 2, 4, 12) vs 9 for Dupixent. Maintenance: 2–4 annual dosing days for zumilokibart (Q12W–Q24W) vs 26 for Dupixent (Q2W). This is the central competitive narrative. For lebrikizumab: induction Q2W × 16 wks (8 doses), then Q4W maintenance (~13/yr). Zumilokibart's dosing advantage applies vs all current AD biologics.

slides.title: Key Efficacy Results at Week 16 (Primary Analysis)

sections.header: Zumilokibart Mid Dose (Planned Phase 3 Dose, N=85) vs Placebo (N=88)
bullets: EASI-75 (primary endpoint): 65.9% vs 23.4% — Δ = 41.9 pp (p<0.001)
I-NRS ≥4pt reduction: 50.5% vs 13.9% — Δ = 36.7 pp (p<0.001)
EASI % change from BL (LS mean): −70.6% vs −34.9% (p<0.001)
Mid and high doses showed similar clinical activity across all endpoints
EASI-75: High 61.6%, Mid 65.9%, Low 50.5%
EASI-90: High 35.8%, Mid 47.4%, Low 28.2%
I-NRS4: High 43.4%, Mid 50.5%, Low 35.7%
Mid dose selected for Phase 3 based on compelling benefit-risk profile
⚠ MCMC-MI imputation — expect 5–10% lower rates with NRI in Phase 3

slides.speakerNotes: All primary and key secondary endpoints were met with high statistical significance. Mid and high doses showed similar activity, while low dose was expectedly lower. IMPORTANT: This is MCMC-MI analysis. In Phase 3 competitor trials using NRI, placebo rates are typically 10-15% for EASI-75 — the 23.4% here likely reflects the more lenient imputation. If the same data were analyzed with NRI, both active and placebo rates would likely be lower.

slides.title: Primary Endpoint: EASI-75 Response Over Time
slides.speakerNotes: EASI-75 time course shows clear dose-response with separation from placebo by Week 2 for all arms. Mid dose (N=85): Wk2 12.2%, Wk4 35.6%, Wk8 52.6%, Wk12 59.7%, Wk16 65.9%. High dose (N=87): 61.6% at Wk16. Low dose (N=86): 50.5% at Wk16. Placebo (N=88): 23.4% at Wk16. All active arms achieved p<0.001 vs placebo. Significance achieved for all treatment arms by Week 2.
slides.disclaimer: Source: Apogee Therapeutics. Review is required before disclosure.

slides.title: EASI Change from Baseline (Continuous Endpoint)
slides.speakerNotes: Percent change in EASI score from baseline (LS mean). Mid dose at Wk16: −70.6% (vs −34.9% PBO). Week 1: −17.0% vs −7.3% (p<0.01) — significant itch and lesion reduction from the very first week. Continuous improvement seen through Week 16 — plateau not yet reached, suggesting further gains at later timepoints. This continuous measure confirms the categorical EASI-75 findings.
slides.disclaimer: Source: Apogee Therapeutics. Review is required before disclosure.

slides.title: IGA 0/1 Response Over Time
slides.speakerNotes: IGA 0/1 with ≥2 point reduction time course. Mid dose at Wk16: 46.0% (vs 10.9% PBO, p<0.001). High dose: 33.4%. Low dose: 27.6%. Clear separation by Week 2 (mid dose 7.1% vs PBO ~0%). Note: Zumilokibart assessed vIGA 0/1 (validated IGA) while competitor trials used IGA 0/1. The validated scale is considered slightly more stringent but generally comparable.
slides.disclaimer: Source: Apogee Therapeutics. Review is required before disclosure.

slides.title: EASI-90 Response Over Time
slides.speakerNotes: EASI-90 time course. Mid dose at Wk16: 47.4% (vs 9.3% PBO, p<0.001). High dose: 35.8%. Low dose: 28.2%. Near-complete clearance showing strong response. Significance by Week 2 for mid dose (5.9%, p<0.05).
slides.disclaimer: Source: Apogee Therapeutics. Review is required before disclosure.

slides.title: I-NRS ≥4-Point Improvement (Itch Response) Over Time
slides.speakerNotes: I-NRS4 (itch reduction ≥4 points from baseline peak ≥4). Mid dose (N=77): Wk2 9.2%, Wk4 19.8%, Wk8 36.2%, Wk12 49.7%, Wk16 50.5%. Placebo (N=84): 13.9% at Wk16. Note: itch significance achieved later than skin endpoints — Wk4 for I-NRS4 vs Wk2 for EASI-75. This is consistent with other anti-IL-13 agents where skin improvement precedes itch relief.
slides.disclaimer: Source: Apogee Therapeutics. Review is required before disclosure.

slides.title: Competitive Comparison: Zumilokibart vs Dupixent Across Endpoints
slides.speakerNotes: Apogee's own cross-trial comparison: zumilokibart mid dose vs Dupixent across 5 endpoints at Wk16. EASI-75: 65.9% vs 49.5% (Δ from PBO: 41.9 vs 36.8). IGA 0/1: 46.0% vs 34.6% (Δ: 34.8 vs 27.8). EASI-90: 47.4% vs 31.8% (Δ: 37.8 vs 25.8). I-NRS4: 50.5% vs 38.4% (Δ: 36.7 vs 27.5). EASI-100: 16.5% vs 5.6%. CAVEATS: Different trials, different populations, different imputation methods (MCMC-MI vs NRI). PBO rates vary (23.4% vs 12.7%).
slides.disclaimer: Cross-trial comparison for illustrative purposes only. Review is required before disclosure.

slides.title: Broader Competitor Landscape: EASI-75 at Week 16
slides.speakerNotes: Cross-trial landscape for EASI-75 at Week 16 across approved and late-stage competitors. Zumilokibart shows numerically highest response among biologics but caveat: Phase 2 MCMC-MI analysis vs Phase 3 NRI for competitors. JAK inhibitors (oral) show higher rates but carry boxed warning. Nemolizumab+TCS is combo therapy — lower Δ reflects high PBO+TCS rate (29.6%).
slides.disclaimer: Cross-trial comparison for illustrative purposes only. Differences in trial design, populations, and endpoints preclude direct comparison. Review is required before disclosure.

slides.title: Competitive EASI-75 Bar Chart (Sponsor Data)
slides.speakerNotes: EASI-75 cross-trial comparison against 4 approved biologics. Zumilokibart 65.9% (N=85, PBO 23.4%). Dupixent 49.5% (N=521, PBO 12.7%, Δ=36.8). Ebglyss/lebrikizumab 53.0% (N=639, PBO 15.3%, Δ=37.7). Nemluvio+TCS (nemolizumab) 42.8% (N=1142, PBO 29.6%, Δ=13.2 — note: combo with TCS). Adbry/tralokinumab 29.1% (N=1192, PBO 12.1%, Δ=17.0). Higher PBO rate for zumilokibart inflates both active and delta.
slides.disclaimer: Cross-trial comparison for illustrative purposes only. Review is required before disclosure.

slides.title: Broader Competitive Landscape: IGA 0/1 at Week 16
slides.speakerNotes: IGA 0/1 cross-trial. Zumilokibart 46.0% (PBO 10.9%, Δ=34.8). Dupixent 34.6% (PBO 6.8%, Δ=27.8). Ebglyss 37.0% (PBO 10.4%, Δ=26.6). Nemluvio+TCS 36.7% (PBO 25.3%, Δ=11.4). Adbry 19.0% (PBO 9.0%, Δ=10.0). Zumilokibart assessed vIGA 0/1 vs IGA 0/1 in competitor trials — slightly different scales.
slides.disclaimer: Cross-trial comparison for illustrative purposes only. Review is required before disclosure.

slides.title: Safety Summary Through Week 16
slides.speakerNotes: Safety profile appears manageable but limited data. Conjunctivitis is the key signal: dose-dependent (10.6% to 20.7%), all in active arms vs 0% PBO. This is higher than lebrikizumab (~7-8% in ADVOCATE). Higher conjunctivitis could become a differentiator favoring lebrikizumab if it persists in Ph3. Overall TEAE rate for mid dose (60%) was lower than placebo (67%), which is reassuring. No effect of ADAs on PK, clinical activity, or safety.
slides.disclaimer: Source: Apogee Therapeutics APEX Part B. Review is required before disclosure.

slides.title: BNMA: EASI-75 — Treatment Effects vs Placebo
interpretation: Zumilokibart mid dose ranks competitively — posterior mean 0.429 [0.323, 0.533], overlapping with dupilumab (0.400) and lebrikizumab Q2W (0.371)
Upadacitinib 30mg leads (0.580); tilrekimig and abrocitinib 200mg also competitive but with wider CrI
All zumilokibart doses show significant effects vs placebo (CrI excludes 0)
Formal indirect comparison does NOT support clear superiority over established biologics — cross-trial bar charts overstate the difference
slides.speakerNotes: BNMA normal-model with 79 treatments from Ph2/Ph3 AD trials on the EASI-75 responder rate difference scale. Zumilokibart mid dose posterior mean of 0.429 overlaps substantially with dupilumab (0.400) and lebrikizumab (0.371). The key insight: once between-study heterogeneity is accounted for, zumilokibart is competitive but NOT clearly superior. Tilrekimig (another IL-13 next-gen from Roche) also ranks high with wide CrI reflecting early-phase data.

slides.title: BNMA: IGA 0/1 — Treatment Effects vs Placebo
interpretation: Lebrikizumab 250mg Q2W has highest posterior mean (0.290) — ranks #1 for IGA 0/1
Zumilokibart low dose ranks #2 (0.236); mid dose ranks #4 (0.145)
Dupilumab and abrocitinib CrI cross 0 — not significantly different from placebo in this IGA 0/1 network
Lilly can use this to counter the 'best-in-class' narrative on IGA 0/1
slides.speakerNotes: IGA 0/1 BNMA from 78-treatment network. Important contrast with cross-trial comparison: lebrikizumab actually ranks #1 for IGA 0/1, despite the press release showing zumilokibart with higher point estimate. This reflects the BNMA's ability to account for heterogeneity in placebo rates. Zumilokibart is competitive but lebrikizumab has a stronger IGA 0/1 signal in the formal network.

slides.title: Head-to-Head vs Lebrikizumab (Lilly)

bullets: Same target: IL-13 neutralization
Same patient population: moderate-to-severe AD
Same endpoint framework (EASI-75, IGA 0/1)
Both SC injection
Both show rapid onset (separation by Wk 2)
Dosing: Q24W (zumi) vs Q2W→Q4W (lebri): 2–4 vs 13 injections/yr
Efficacy (cross-trial): EASI-75 65.9% vs 53.0% — MCMC-MI vs NRI caveat
BNMA: overlapping posteriors; no significant separation
Phase: Ph2 Part B (zumi) vs Ph3 + approved (lebri)
Conjunctivitis: 10.6% (zumi mid) vs ~7–8% (lebri Ph3)
Safety database: N=85 (zumi) vs >1000 (lebri)
Label: none (zumi) vs broad AD label (lebri)

slides.speakerNotes: Zumilokibart wins on convenience (dosing interval) and numerically on efficacy in cross-trial bars. Lebrikizumab wins on evidence maturity: approved, Phase 3 data with standard NRI, growing real-world evidence. The BNMA shows overlapping posteriors. Key uncertainty: will Ph3 with NRI confirm Ph2 MCMC-MI numbers?

slides.title: Key Takeaways & Implications for Lilly
takeaways: Zumilokibart achieved numerically best EASI-75 (65.9%) and IGA 0/1 (46.0%) at Wk16 — but Ph2 with MCMC-MI imputation
Extended dosing (Q24W maintenance, 2–4 injections/year) is a powerful commercial differentiator vs all AD biologics
BNMA shows competitive but overlapping efficacy with lebrikizumab — no clear statistical separation
Conjunctivitis rate 10.6–20.7% (dose-dependent) is higher than lebrikizumab (~7–8%) — potential Lilly advantage
Timeline: ADventure Phase 3 initiation 2H 2026 → readout ~2028 → regulatory filing ~2029 earliest
actions: Monitor ADventure Phase 3 design: NRI vs MCMC-MI, sample size, comparator arm
Leverage BNMA indirect comparison to counter cross-trial bar chart narrative (show overlapping CrIs)
Strengthen lebrikizumab positioning on safety (lower conjunctivitis), real-world evidence, and label breadth
Prepare materials comparing dosing convenience vs certainty of efficacy (Phase 3 data vs Phase 2)
Assess BNMA update once Phase 3 data available
slides.speakerNotes: Bottom line: zumilokibart is the most credible emerging threat to lebrikizumab in the anti-IL-13 space. The convenience story is powerful. However, Lilly has a 2-3 year head start, approved label, robust Ph3 data, and possibly a lower conjunctivitis rate. The BNMA does not support clear superiority. Key question: will Ph3 NRI confirm Ph2 numbers? Monitor closely.
